task_summary: Repair first-turn admission and safe steering handoff in an isolated candidate, validate it and flash after renewed owner authorization.

acceptance: Verified target build, flash and stationary configuration
completed: Isolated repair preserves frozen baselines and separates build, flash and live identities.
Passed segmented/fault checks, eight full-lap cases and all state-handoff audits under unchanged limits.
Completed clean official target build, verified official flash and stationary wired/wireless identity.
Saved and attributed both first physical trials; identified repeated outgoing-lane relock timeout without changing protections.
Reproduced the outgoing recovery/speed coupling defect in an unchanged host controller; recorded incomplete restoration of stable turning parameters.
Rejected an unpowered manual distance sample and stopped measurement after the owner reported a rollback to an old stable version.
remaining: Physical acceptance failed twice; fixes for the demonstrated controller regression are not implemented.
Current owner-restored firmware identity is unverified; powered odometry and camera distance calibration are not completed.

observations: A candidate that completed eight laps still had unsafe steering handoffs; state-transition auditing prevented its release.
Intermediate relock designs rejected correct lanes or missed adjacent corners; bounded raw optical evidence and explicit controller ownership resolved the tested cases.
A GUI-dependent auxiliary project builder blocked official headless compilation; isolated metadata-only correction enabled the licensed build.
Owner deferred flashing overnight; wall-clock duration must not be interpreted as active implementation time.
One coordinator prepared local handoffs; no peer acceptance is claimed.
Both physical runs stopped at the first-turn exit despite correct target heading; passing modeled laps did not establish physical lane alignment.
Owner reports old firmware turns normally on the old map. This raises software-regression priority but is not a controlled software-only A/B because the map also changed.
Reading an open capture file directory length as zero incorrectly led to repeated serial reconnects despite existing raw bytes. A later device disappearance is a separate event.
Successful historical turn behavior was not completely restored: changed turn gain and ceiling survived while strict exit relock was added without matching low-speed recovery.

recommendations.action: Keep per-transition safety audits alongside lap completion metrics, including initial admission and fault/coast checks.
recommendations.next_check: Compare the first physical turn and exit with saved diagnostic evidence without relaxing acceptance limits.

recommendations.action: Preflight auxiliary GUI-dependent builders before clean official headless builds; preserve compiler options and record metadata diff.
recommendations.next_check: Apply only when the same builder is present; confirm a fresh full source compilation.

recommendations.action: Validate diagnostic decoders on short and saturated records, isolate textual record envelopes from multiplexed binary data, and attribute record completion before later launches.
recommendations.next_check: Use the saved two short physical records and the saturated fixture as capture/decoder regression inputs.

recommendations.action: Treat the successful effective controller profile as a regression baseline; separate hardware, route and safety changes and replay real failed exits before broad simulation.
recommendations.next_check: Demonstrate low-speed bounded recovery and safe handoff on both recorded failure states without weakening quality or protection limits.

recommendations.action: Use bytes actually read and timestamped parsed samples for connection status; distinguish telemetry omission from device disappearance and require a powered stationary cumulative baseline before manual pushes.
recommendations.next_check: When measurement resumes, obtain a valid baseline with main power on before instructing movement; do not integrate sparse velocity telemetry as exact totals.
